cim: Congress faces year-end deadline for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence legislation
cim_eredeti: Congress faces year-end deadline for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence legislation
szoveg_eredeti:
Cybersecurity protections and artificial intelligence oversight remain at the forefront of the legislative agenda as lawmakers return to Washington with limited time to finalize critical policy measures before the end of the year, as first reported by Nextgov.

The legislative session is dominated by a Dec. 11 deadline for the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015, which provides legal protections for companies sharing threat data with the government. Lawmakers are also considering the renewal of the Federal Cybersecurity Enhancement Act and the Technology Modernization Fund. These provisions are currently being debated as part of the broader National Defense Authorization Act, which has faced procedural hurdles in the Senate. Beyond infrastructure, Congress is evaluating several artificial intelligence proposals, including the FRONTIER Act and the AI Kill Switch Act, which aim to mandate safety disclosures and emergency shutdown capabilities for advanced models. These discussions follow high-profile security incidents involving AI labs. Additionally, the session may address the status of Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, an intelligence-gathering authority that lapsed earlier this year. With a transition in congressional leadership approaching in January, the current session represents a final opportunity to secure these protections and establish regulatory frameworks for emerging technologies.
